Switching to charcoal is a great choice for that classic smoky flavor, and keeping the temperature steady is definitely the key to a stress-free cook. The most effective method is setting up a **two-zone fire**. Instead of spreading the coals evenly across the bottom, pile them on only one side of the grill. This creates a "hot zone" for direct searing and a "cool zone" on the other side where you can place food for indirect cooking.

To control the temperature, manage the air vents. Think of the vents as the throttle of your grill: opening them more lets in more oxygen, which makes the fire burn hotter, while closing them restricts oxygen and lowers the heat. For a steady low-and-slow cook, keep the bottom vents partially open and adjust the top vent to maintain your desired range. If the fire starts to die down, you can add a few fresh, lit coals to the hot zone without disrupting the entire setup. Using a good quality charcoal chimney starter also gives you a consistent base of fully lit coals to begin with, which helps stabilize the temperature from the start.
